chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Noble Sissle as entertainer and employer
summary: Briggs describes Sissle as a fine, educated, fair man who paid what he owed but whose spending wife cost him heavily.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, what kind of a guy was Sissle? He was a pretty industrious guy?
Yes, he was a wonderful entertainer. Very intelligent.
Singer, yes. He was an entertainer, singer, and actor. You've heard of Sissle and Blake?
Well, he did the singing, with Blake at the piano.

And Sissle was one of our most fortunate boys, he had a very, very fine education, and he knew people, and he knew how to take care of himself, and how to treat people and everything. He was a fine person.
He was a very fine man. I had no difficulties with him at all.
He was fair, he was fair, when he promised you a certain sum, he'd pay you. He paid me what he owed me.
Sissle, he was a songwriter, as you know --
And he had money coming in from it.
He needed all that money, because his domestic affairs caught him -- he had to have plenty of money to cope with --
No, no, he just had one that I know of, but she cost him a whole lot of money.
She used to drink as much -- I mean she stayed ossified, you see.
And not only that, but buying clothes, and everything -- debts, making debts on her husband's name at the bank.
